questions.question: When merging into traffic while driving a double or triple, a driver should:

options.text: Assume there is enough space for the vehicle to merge.
Make sure there is extra space for the vehicle to merge.
Wait to merge until there is no traffic in the lane for at least two miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is extra space for the vehicle to merge.
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are larger than smaller vehicles and need more space to merge into traffic. They also need a longer distance to speed up.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road:

options.text: Usually do not contain moisture, so they cannot freeze.
Will stay slippery after ice on other areas of the road has melted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will stay slippery after ice on other areas of the road has melted.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas stay cooler longer because they get less sunlight. Ice in these areas can remain slippery after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed:
questions.correctAnswerText: By at least one-half.
questions.explanation: When driving on packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more. Slippery surfaces make it hard to stop or turn, so you must slow down to drive safely.

questions.question: If you must write a vehicle inspection report, you should sign it:

options.text: Only if defects were found and repairs were completed.
Only if repairs are estimated to cost more than $1,000.
Only if a law enforcement officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and repairs were completed.
questions.explanation: Sign the previous vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and repairs have been completed or are not needed.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take for a 200-pound person to reach a 0.02 percent blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects you before you reach the legal limit. A 200-pound person reaches a BAC of 0.02 percent after just one drink.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: An axle brake system
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will come on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will come on.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a warning light activates if pressure drops below 60 psi. This warning may also be a wig wag device.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if the green lever on the control panel is pushed down.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in an air brake system, there is a delay of half a second or more as air travels through the lines to activate the brakes. This is different from hydraulic brakes in cars and light trucks, which work immediately.

questions.question: What is the smallest allowed size for a hazardous materials placard?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 ¾ square inches
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you do not get enough sleep
When you want to take a nap
The amount of time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you do not get enough sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt builds up when you do not sleep enough. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: When checking a coupling under the trailer, you should:

options.text: Remove the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the emergency position.
Look at the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When checking a coupling, go under the trailer and look at the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: If you park on the side of a road, you should:

options.text: Stand in the road and wave your arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is very important at night.

questions.question: You can identify a converter dolly with ABS by looking for:

options.text: A yellow light on the left side of the dolly.
A blue light on the left side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light on the left side of the dolly.
questions.explanation: Dollies made after March 1, 1998 must have anti-lock brakes. A dolly with anti-lock brakes has a yellow light on its left side.

questions.question: Improper coupling is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Drivers must know how to connect and disconnect trailers correctly. Bad coupling and disconnection can cause serious accidents.

questions.question: What causes the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.correctAnswerText: Rearward amplification
questions.explanation: Vehicles with trailers can roll over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect, which is caused by rearward amplification. Different vehicles have different levels of rearward amplification, so drivers need to understand their vehicle's behavior.

questions.question: Retreaded tires:

options.text: Can be used anywhere on a bus.
Can be used on the front of a bus.
Can be used on the rear of a bus.
Cannot be used on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded or recapped tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how do you know if the anti-lock brake system is broken?

options.text: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the trailer flashes three times and then stays on.
All rear lights on the trailer flash and then turn off.
The blue light near the driver's door lights up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with anti-lock brakes have a yellow warning light on the left rear. If this light stays on after you start the engine, the anti-lock brake system is not working.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
Only the rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: At the start of a trip, open all shut-off valves except the rear valves on the last trailer. This allows air to reach all brakes while stopping air from escaping the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these is a required emergency item?
questions.correctAnswerText: Spare electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher; spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers); and warning devices for parked vehicles, like reflective triangles.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A low air pressure warning device
A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A sound made by air brakes
A part that lets air move freely in the braking system

questions.correctAnswerText: A low air pressure warning device
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device in an air brake system. When air pressure drops below 60 psi, it drops a mechanical arm into your view.
